en.headline: Parking meter operator to pay HK$1.3 million over citywide outage
en.dek: Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said the operator will pay about HK$1.3 million and refund users after a software update disabled roughly 11,000 meters on November 3.
body: The operator of Hong Kong’s on-street parking meter system has agreed to pay the government about HK$1.3 million after a four-hour outage earlier this month, Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan told the Legislative Council on Wednesday.

Chan said a software update carried out in the early hours of November 3 contained a flaw that prevented the backend system from communicating with about 11,000 meters across the city. The Transport Department, Electrical and Mechanical Services Department and Digital Policy Office reviewed the operator’s report and found no hardware failure, network attack or data leak.

The operator has arranged to refund fees charged during the outage and has strengthened monitoring and testing procedures. Chan said the Transport Department will conduct its next security risk assessment in December.

zh.headline: 咪錶營辦商就全城故障向政府賠償約130萬元
zh.dek: 運輸及物流局局長陳美寶在立法會表示，營辦商將向政府賠償約130萬元，並向受影響市民退還事故期間收費。
body: 運輸及物流局局長陳美寶周三在立法會表示，路旁咪錶系統營辦商已承諾就本月初的全城故障向政府賠償約130萬元。
陳美寶指出，11月3日清晨的軟件更新程式存有缺陷，導致後台系統未能與全港約1.1萬部咪錶正常連接。運輸署、機電工程署及數字政策辦公室審視報告後確認，事件並非硬件故障、網絡攻擊或資料外洩所致。
營辦商已安排向受影響使用者退還事故期間的收費，並加強實時監測及測試程序。陳美寶表示，運輸署將於12月進行下一輪全面保安風險評估。
